Hook: The Foreign Police has moved
Tip: Since 18 May 2026, Bratislava's Foreign Police is at Račianska 62 (Nové Mesto), not Regrútska 4. Older guides may still show the old address.
Sticker question: Where is the Bratislava Foreign Police now?

Hook: 8 days. That's your insurance deadline.
Tip: Register with a health insurer within 8 days of starting a job, a živnosť or permanent residence. Late? Fines up to €3,319 – plus full price for care in the gap.
Sticker question: How long do you have to register?

Hook: Open your IBAN before you land
Tip: Slovak banks need in-person verification, but Revolut or Wise open remotely from home. Slovak payroll accepts any EU IBAN – so you're set for payday.

Hook: Register your živnosť online – it's free
Tip: A free-trade živnosť (voľná) costs €0 via slovensko.sk vs €7 in person. You'll need a Slovak eID with a chip.

Hook: Airbnb won't get you a permit
Tip: For a non-EU residence permit you need a lease with notarised owner signatures – or the owner's notarised consent. It's the most common stumbling block, so sort it first.

Hook: Why you'll still want an SK IBAN
Tip: Some landlords and utilities still prefer a Slovak IBAN for direct debits. Employed? Ask HR – if your employer works with Tatra banka, opening an account is usually fast-tracked.

Hook: Don't speak Slovak? Start with Union
Tip: Slovakia has 3 public insurers: VšZP, Dôvera and Union. Union is currently the only one with fully English online registration. Tell HR your pick – otherwise VšZP is typically the default.

Hook: The “first year free” rule is gone
Tip: Since 1 Jan 2026, new self-employed pay social insurance from the 1st day of the 6th month (start in March → pay from 1 Sept). You begin on the reduced mikroodvod, about €131.34/month.
Sticker question: First živnosť year = no social insurance?

Hook: EU citizen? Register by day 120
Tip: Staying longer than 90 days? Register your residence within the next 30 days – roughly by day 120. It's free, but in person only: no online, email or proxy.

Hook: Want a specialist? Start with a GP
Tip: Register with a GP (obvodný lekár) – you need a referral to see a specialist. Emergency care needs no referral.

Hook: 183 days here = Slovak tax resident
Tip: Spend 183+ days in Slovakia in a calendar year (or have a permanent home here) and you're a tax resident. That means Slovakia taxes your worldwide income.
Sticker question: How many days make you a tax resident?

Hook: No receipts? Use the 60% rule
Tip: Freelancers can deduct flat-rate expenses: 60% of income, capped at €20,000 a year – no receipts needed. Do the maths both ways; it's often the cheaper option.
Sticker question: How much do you love keeping receipts?

Hook: Got your card? 30-day countdown starts
Tip: Within 30 days of collecting your residence card, give the Foreign Police a medical report. It can't be older than 30 days.

Hook: Insurance card not here yet? No panic
Tip: Your coverage starts when you register – the card is just proof. Ask your insurer for a potvrdenie o poistení; doctors and hospitals accept it immediately.

Hook: Only employed? Let your employer do it
Tip: Ask your employer for the annual reconciliation (ročné zúčtovanie) by mid-February – done. You only file yourself if you have other income, like rent, foreign income or a živnosť.

Hook: New s.r.o. rules since 17 August 2026
Tip: Your founding deed now needs a notary or a lawyer – verified signatures aren't enough. Exception: the simplified e-form (max 5 shareholders, free trades only).

Hook: Tax return due 31 March
Tip: File and pay last year's tax by 31 March. Need more time? A simple notification moves it to 30 June – or 30 September with foreign income.
Sticker question: When is the tax return due?

Hook: Renewing? Start 90 days early
Tip: File before your permit expires – realistically start 90 days ahead, as slots fill fast (especially Sept–Oct). Keep your podací lístok: it proves you're legal while you wait.
Sticker question: How stressful was your last Foreign Police visit?

Hook: Leaving Slovakia? Your pension stays yours
Tip: Your Slovak insurance years stay on record. With at least 1 year here, Slovakia pays its share at retirement – and you apply from wherever you live.

Hook: Your s.r.o. pays tax even at a loss
Tip: Every s.r.o. pays a minimum tax (daňová licencia) – €340/year if taxable income is up to €50,000. Good news: not for the year it's set up.
